mappings.applicability_reason: The retrieval index stores content that is later retrieved and placed into model context at answer time, and the corpus is populated from more than one source (the help-center repository and the support platform's resolved-tickets export) [evd-002, evd-012], so the requirement governing the retrieval corpus's write path applies to compromise of the managed index.

Resolved support tickets have a documented two-year retention schedule on the support platform [evd-004] and are embedded into the retrieval index via the ingestion pipeline [evd-002, evd-012], so this threat engages the requirement that the retrieval index follow its sources' lifecycle.

The retrieval index is a managed vector database that stores embeddings derived from workspace support tickets and other non-public content [evd-002, evd-012], and it is reached over a network boundary the team does not control, so encryption in transit and at rest for this data is in scope for this threat.

Customer support-ticket content is embedded and stored in a managed vector-database offering that the team did not build [evd-002, evd-012], so customer data crosses to an external provider whose retention and usage terms affect the impact of a compromise of that service.

The retrieval index is an internal data store, not itself a public interface, and it holds embeddings for many workspaces in a shared index [evd-002]; it is described as reachable only from the answer service's network segment [evd-012], so the requirement that such internal components be reachable only from the workloads that use them applies to this threat.

documentation_gaps.title: Encryption for retrieval index embeddings at rest and in transit is not documented
documentation_gaps.description: The retrieval index is a managed vector database holding embeddings of help-center articles and resolved support tickets for all workspaces in a shared index [evd-002], and it is described as the only copy of the embeddings and as reachable only from the answer service's network segment [evd-012]. The documentation does not state whether connections to this managed service use transport encryption or whether data at rest (including any provider-managed backups) is encrypted and by whom, so it is not possible to determine from the current material whether req-DATA-001 is satisfied for the embeddings stored in the index.
documentation_gaps.importance: Clarifying how embeddings in the retrieval index are protected in transit and at rest is necessary to assess how much a compromise of the managed vector-database platform or its storage deviates from the system's baseline expectations for protecting customer support history.
requested_evidence: Managed vector-database configuration or provider documentation stating encryption-at-rest guarantees for the standard tier and who manages the keys.
Documentation or configuration showing whether connections from the answer service to the managed vector database are protected by TLS or an equivalent transport-encryption mechanism.

documentation_gaps.title: Provider retention and usage terms for retrieval index embeddings are not documented
documentation_gaps.description: Architecture and operations documentation describe what content is embedded and stored in the managed vector database [evd-002, evd-012] and note that resolved support tickets are retained on the support platform for two years and then deleted under an agreed retention schedule [evd-004]. However, the material does not state the managed vector-database provider's data-retention period for embeddings and metadata, whether provider-managed backups persist beyond application-side deletion, or whether the provider may use embeddings for purposes beyond serving Relay Answers. This prevents determining whether external-processor data-handling expectations in req-TPI-001 and lifecycle expectations in req-RAG-003 are met for the retrieval index.
documentation_gaps.importance: Understanding how long the managed vector-database provider retains embeddings and whether it uses them beyond serving Relay Answers is directly relevant to the impact of a compromise of the retrieval index and to whether derived embeddings respect the two-year retention commitment for support tickets.
requested_evidence: A summary of the managed vector-database provider's data-retention and usage terms for the standard tier, including any training or analytics use of stored embeddings.

Documentation stating how long embeddings and their backups are retained in the retrieval index and how that period relates to the two-year retention of resolved support tickets on the support platform.
Any configuration or operational procedure that removes or anonymizes embeddings when their source tickets age out or are deleted.
